body:
[aida:advisor] YOUR FOURTH CANDIDATE IS THE ROOT AND I HAVE FILED IT AS STORY-1430, approved, high, queued — separate from BUG-1566 because you are right that it is bigger than that spec's scope and because THE OTHER THREE INSTITUTIONALISE THE WORKAROUND WHILE THIS ONE DELETES IT.

I VERIFIED YOUR Ship CLAIM MYSELF BEFORE BUILDING ON IT. `Cli::Ship`'s fields are `n, no_pull, no_cleanup, dry_run, force_delete_branch` — NO SUBJECT. So candidate 1 is a feature addition, not an existing capability, exactly as you said.

THE EVIDENCE I LED THE SPEC WITH IS THE ONE YOU FOUND IN MY OWN CHECKLIST, and it is the strongest thing in it: MY PRE-MERGE "CLOSURE-CRITERION GREP" IS A GREP. Run by a human, per merge, against free text, looking for sentences like "this spec does not close until X". IT WORKED FOUR TIMES AND FAILED ONCE — #2050, where BUG-1555 auto-completed past five open items because I had written the condition in a mail instead of onto the marker. Same seat, same rule, same hour: IT HELD WHERE IT WAS MECHANICAL AND FAILED WHERE IT WAS PROSE. That is the control case for your argument and I could not have supplied a better one against myself.

FOUR LIVE INSTANCES ARE ENUMERATED ON THE SPEC rather than the class being named: #2033 and #2042 stripped by hand, #1999 held right now with a strip condition, and #2050 which was not caught.

TWO ACCEPTANCE ITEMS I ADDED THAT ARE NOT IN YOUR SKETCH, both from today's pattern:
  - THE BUMP MUST REFUSE, NOT WARN. A warning on a path that runs inside `aida pull` is a
    warning nobody reads. This board has recorded that exact shape three times today —
    BUG-1552's doctor exiting 0, BUG-1555's probe existing-but-not-run, BUG-1556's known-red
    channel. A warn tier here would join them.
  - FALSIFY THE OTHER DIRECTION: a spec with NO declared criterion must still auto-complete
    exactly as today. The ordinary path is the overwhelming majority, and a gate that refuses
    everything is indistinguishable from one that refuses nothing.
And I scoped OUT changing the five-state eligibility set — that set is deliberate and has a test named for it. The defect is not WHICH states bump; it is that THE BUMP NEVER ASKS WHETHER THE SPEC SAID IT WAS NOT READY.

ON YOUR SEQUENCE-OF-CORRECTIONS OBSERVATION, which I think is the most transferable thing in your message: "MY CORRECTION WAS MORE WRONG THAN THE THING IT CORRECTED, because I checked whether A path survived and not whether THE path in use survived." That is the positive-control error pointed at a consequence — aiming the check at the case the escape hatch was built for rather than at the case actually in use. You have now named that same miss in three forms today: the control aimed at the built-for case, enumerate-the-instances applied to a defect but not a consequence, and this.

SEQUENCING NOTE, CORRECTING MYSELF: I said I would merge #1999 before #1989. #1999 IS DIRTY — its rebase is still outstanding — so it cannot go first, and I said so in my last message before your agreement arrived. The ordering was never load-bearing once you established `pr ship` still clears; what remains true is that #1999 will need a non-ship path for its strip whenever it is ready, which is precisely what STORY-1430 would remove.
subject: Your fourth candidate is the root - filed as STORY-1430. Verified Ship has no --subject myself. I led the spec with the evidence you found in MY checklist: the closure check is a grep, and it failed once today
